findings.title: The mandatory redaction inventory regression still expects sixteen owner classes
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The normal mandatory release test suite fails deterministically at the frozen source.
findings.reproduction: Build the frozen source, then run node docs/audits/AUD-032-harnesses/reproduce-regressions.mjs, or the existing S022 inventory case directly. It reads current src declarations with public/static data only.
findings.expected: The maintained inventory regression accounts for every intended current Redacted owner and the mandatory suite passes without deleting its coverage check.
findings.observed: The existing assertion expects 16 labels, while the actual source scan returns 28. The additional labels are CandidateListWriter, CardValues, EncodeCardExport, InputBytes, MarkedReading, PreparedWalletEvidence, PrivateResult, ReadingSpace, SecretValue, ShareCardSet, ShareExport and ShareValues. It fails in both the full disjoint-file run and the exact focused rerun.
findings.impact: Release verification is red after the ownership refactor. This is a stale regression inventory, not evidence that those classes disclose secrets: the inherited String/JSON/inspect control passes in the ordinary file and current owner tests are separate.
findings.prerequisites: Current source and existing installed pinned toolchain; no private input, network or special OS condition.
findings.recommendedFix: In a separately authorized remediation, reconcile the explicit owner inventory with all current classes and preserve a meaningful completeness/redaction oracle. Do not remove the assertion or drop new owners merely to make the suite green.
findings.requiredVerification: See the original inventory assertion fail before the fix and pass afterwards; preserve String, JSON and inspect refusal behavior and current secret-owner tests, then rerun the normal mandatory suite.
findings.relationship: The ownership refactor introduced new classes, but this is a distinct stale test inventory. It does not reopen the prior verified producer cleanup finding.

findings.title: The mandatory share-QR export regression asserts an obsolete success message
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The normal mandatory release test suite fails deterministically before its share-image count and recovery assertions.

affectedFiles.role: Current supported success wording, not a demonstrated runtime fault

findings.reproduction: Run the existing test named saves the QR code of the sheets as images beside the PDF, which restore and decode read, or the published focused reproduction harness. Its public all-zero BIP39 phrase reaches a successful real protected encode --sskr command.
findings.expected: A valid share export proceeds to the real three-image and quorum-recovery assertions, and the mandatory regression matches the supported success contract.
findings.observed: The child exits 0 and reports Saved the QR codes of the share sheets as images beside them: 3 PNG files. The test still requires Saved the QR code of each share's sheets as an image beside them: 3 PNG files. It fails twice at the wording assertion before testing the files and restoration.
findings.impact: The release suite is red and this test no longer reaches its intended QR recovery oracle. A separate current production-path media control actually produced three share PNGs and restored the exact public phrase from members 1 and 3, so this finding does not allege lost or unreadable QR backups.
findings.prerequisites: Current build, bundled public artwork and existing pinned dependencies; no private inputs.
findings.recommendedFix: In separately authorized remediation, reconcile the expected success text or assert its meaningful count/output contract without weakening the existing real file-count and exact quorum-recovery checks.
findings.requiredVerification: Keep the original red assertion evidence, make this current public production-path case pass, require three share PNGs and exact recovery from members 1 and 3, and rerun the normal mandatory suite.

findings.title: The security policy names randomBytes instead of the production randomFillSync adapter
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Documentation precision only; both named Node APIs use the cryptographic random source.
findings.reproduction: Read the last SSKR integrity/randomness sentence in SECURITY.md and follow nodeFillRandom through the actual Node split callers. No runtime or wallet input is required.
findings.expected: The security policy's named production API agrees with its implementation.
findings.observed: The policy says the share random numbers come from Node crypto.randomBytes; nodeFillRandom actually calls randomFillSync on the supplied buffer.
findings.impact: A reader tracing the documented source looks for the wrong API. No insecure fallback, reduced entropy, changed wire format or cryptographic weakness is demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Correct the one API name in a separately authorized documentation change, or describe the cryptographic source without an incorrect function name.
findings.requiredVerification: Compare the corrected sentence with the current adapter; preserve the existing production randomness and nearest split/refusal tests. No new RNG or cryptographic campaign is required.
